SWITCHES AT RUN TIME
- Clarity.set(id, bool): flips a switch. Hooks, listeners, ticks, pointer and appear callbacks stop or resume at once. CSS follows at once.
- Clarity.onToggle(id, fn(on)): callbacks so an item can undo or redo inline state when its switch flips.
- Setting Clarity.on.Gn = false by hand also works, except for onToggle; CSS then follows within 250 ms.
- Clarity.item(id, setupFn): runs setupFn once at load, only if the switch is on, inside try/catch.

HOOKS (use these instead of wrapping a game function): Clarity.hook(point, id, { before(call), after(call), order })
- Points, each wrapped ONCE by the core and outermost over every game wrapper: 'UI.actions', 'UI.closeActions', 'UI.bigIcon', 'UI.pulseMoods', 'UI.bubble', 'UI.update', 'Audio2.blip', 'onTap', 'hitTest', 'interact', 'currentActivity', 'onEnterRoomBy', 'checkMess', 'showWish', 'openIsoMap', 'drawProp', 'drawExitSigns', 'featTick'. Clarity.points() lists them.
- call = { name, self, args, result, skip }.
- before(call) may set call.skip = true, and call.result if needed, so the game's own function is not called. The first skip stops the remaining before-hooks.
- after(call) runs after the game's function. It also runs after a skip, so check call.skip. It may replace call.result.
- In both, this === call.self. Never mutate call.args.
- order: lower runs first (default 0); equal orders run in registration order.
- Hooks run only while Clarity.on[id] is true.
- A hook that throws is reported once (console.warn 'clarity: Gn before X') and its changes to skip/result are undone.
- With nothing registered, or every hook switched off, the wrapper is exactly the game's call: same this, arguments and return value.
- Clarity.inner(point): the game's own function under the hooks. Call it to bypass every clarity hook, e.g. to replay a deferred icon: Clarity.inner('UI.bigIcon')(ch, ms).
- drawExitSigns: builder.js:234 re-wraps it once on the next frame. The core's wrapper sits inside builder's and still runs exactly once per frame (measured 60/s). Never re-wrap anything yourself.
- Not hook points:
  - ui.js internals: actions() and openPanel() call the private closeActions; placeActs is private. Use local edits (G6, G7).
  - askReq is private to fun.js. Use a local edit (G31) or Clarity.appear('#reqBtn').
  - changeRoom: use the 'room' event.
  - say: G22 is a static table.
  - resize and the camera: only the layout worker changes framing, through engine.js:169, game.js:286 and calls to resize() and render() by name.
- Example: Clarity.hook('checkMess', 'G2', { order: 10, before(c) { if (Clarity.busyNow() || Clarity.quietFor() < 10) c.skip = true; } });
- Example: Clarity.hook('hitTest', 'G8', { order: 10, after(c) { const h = c.result; if (h && h.kind === 'prop') c.result = see(h, c.args[0], c.args[1]); } });

EVENTS: Clarity.listen(evt, id, fn)
- 'room' (was, room): after every real room change. Dispatched from a Floors.hooks entry, i.e. from floors.js's changeRoom, which is the outermost one.
- 'screenOpen' / 'screenClose': Clarity.screenOpen() turned true / false.
- 'activityStart' / 'activityEnd': Clarity.busyNow() turned true / false. On activityEnd, Clarity.endedAt = E.t (game seconds).
- The start of a game (the title closing) is a screenClose and an activityEnd.
- Edges are sampled every 100 ms, and also synchronously whenever Clarity.quietFor() or Clarity.sample() is called, so an edge fires once, never late for a reader.
- Example: Clarity.listen('activityEnd', 'G1', () => { lastInput = E.t; });

TIMER: Clarity.every(ms, id, fn(nowMs))
- One shared 50 ms setInterval. fn runs at most every ms (minimum 50) while the switch is on.
- Example: Clarity.every(100, 'G15', tick);

TOUCHES: Clarity.pointer('down' | 'up', id, fn(event))
- One window capture listener per type (passive), installed on first use. It runs before any game handler sees the event.
- Look only: never preventDefault or stopPropagation.
- Example: Clarity.pointer('down', 'G1', () => { lastInput = E.t; });

NEW NODES: Clarity.appear(selector, id, fn(node))
- One MutationObserver on body (childList, subtree), installed on first use.
- fn runs as a microtask, before paint, for every added element matching selector, whether it is the added node itself or inside an added subtree.
- The node may already be gone again, so check isConnected.
- Example: Clarity.appear('.stk-toast', 'G27', t => { if (Clarity.screenOpen()) { t.style.display = 'none'; queue.push(t.textContent); } });

STATE HELPERS
- Clarity.bodyBusy(): marina.state is swing, bars, ride or wheel, or a looping anim. False before the game exists.
- Clarity.screenOpen(): any of the following is up:
  - the title;
  - any #panel screen, including the map, the fort builder and interior, Lego/tiles, the shelf, pool, films, stuffies, spa, tree climb and the builder;
  - Studio.active, #storyBox or #stkBox.
  The TV and the fort tray are not screens.
- Clarity.busyNow(): inActivity() || bodyBusy().
- Clarity.quietFor(): game seconds since the last activity ended. 0 while one is going on; Infinity before any ended.
- Clarity.endedAt: E.t of the last activity end (null before). Clarity.sample(): re-evaluate the edges now.
- Clarity.playing(): marina exists and the title is hidden.
- Clarity.landscape(): innerWidth > innerHeight.

GEOMETRY HELPERS
- Clarity.hudRects(st?, opt?) returns [[x0,y0,x1,y1], weight, kind, element] for every visible HUD control.
  - Kinds: strip (#roombar .rb), pill (#floorpill .fl:not(.off)), map, arrow (.navarrow:not(.off)), weather (#weatherBtn:not(.hidden)), alert (#alerts .alertb), face (.facecard.show), stop (#stopBtn:not(.hidden)), book and dress (not .off), wish, req, give (#fx .pichint), call (.cm-call), mood (#moodbar .mood), moodToggle.
  - Skipped: zero-size controls, visibility:hidden, and opacity < 0.05 on the control or an ancestor.
  - Weight 4. In landscape, mood and moodToggle get weight 6 and are widened 8 px to the left.
  - Coordinates are relative to st (a DOMRect, e.g. placeActs' stage rect) or to #stage. opt.client gives viewport coordinates.
  - opt.kinds and opt.except filter by kind.
  - Cached 250 ms (dropped on resize and orientationchange). opt.fresh measures now.
  - Controls outside the picture (the tall-portrait dock, the portrait mood row) are included; they overlap nothing in it.
  - Example (G6): if (window.Clarity && Clarity.is('G6')) { acts.hud = acts.hud || Clarity.hudRects(st, { fresh: true }); for (const x of acts.hud) avoid.push(x); }
- Clarity.stageRect(): #stage's DOMRect, cached 250 ms.
- Clarity.toClient(wx, wy) gives viewport px. Clarity.fromClient(cx, cy) gives world coordinates.
- Clarity.onCanvas(cx, cy): elementFromPoint there is #cv, i.e. nothing covers the picture at that point.
- Clarity.overlap(a, b): overlap area of two [x0,y0,x1,y1] rects.
- Clarity.nudgeX(box, rects, { gap = 4, max, bounds: [minX, maxX] }) returns the smallest sideways shift in px that clears every rect at the box's height (hudRects entries or plain rects), or null if none within max.
  - Example: const dx = Clarity.nudgeX(b, Clarity.hudRects(null, { except: ['give', 'call'] }), { max: 62, bounds: [0, st.width] });
- Clarity.floorLevel(room): main 0, up +1, basement -1, outside 0, tree houses 0.5, unknown rooms 0.
- Clarity.floorDir(from, to): +1 up, -1 down, 0 same level.
  - Example (G39): const fd = window.Clarity && Clarity.is('G39') ? Clarity.floorDir(prev, G.room) : 0;

MOTION HELPER
- Clarity.shake(el, { px = 4, ms = 150, times = 2 }) returns an Animation or null.
- It is a side-shake on the individual translate property only, with composite 'add'. Without composite support it starts from the element's computed translate.
- So transforms, CSS animations, :active scales and centring translates keep working, and a CSS animation:none cannot cancel it.
- Example: Clarity.shake(btn); Audio2.blip(-12, 'triangle', 0.08, 0.1);

MISC
- Clarity.warnOnce(key, err).
- Item state and item helpers live on Clarity.Gn, e.g. Clarity.G18 = { target: null } and Clarity.G23 = { hintGap() {...} }. Never on G, never in localStorage.

issues.problem: ui.js:52's choice handler runs UI.closeActions() before a.fn(). A choice that opens a screen therefore opens it immediately after the hook returns. Measured with the dining table's 🎨 (critic/g27_closeorder.js): screenOpen() is false inside the hook and true when the same tap handler returns. A replay inside the hook plays 💎✨ under the screen, where it expires unseen. That breaks 'never dropped' and the check 'treasure then a choice that opens the studio: the icon appears once, after the studio closes'.
issues.fix: Never replay synchronously in the hook. Schedule it with setTimeout 0 or the next tick, re-check screenOpen(), and otherwise wait for screenClose. The same applies when G2's screenOpen listener calls UI.closeActions().

Yet the entry keeps the draft's once-per-30 s far-mew limit and only grafts on the child's always-paws rule. That is inconsistent with how G18, G22, G23 and G24 were reconciled (single-lens amendments applied in full). It always returned the smallest shift in either direction. G17 and G26 require 'sideways only, toward the room's centre'.

ui.js also closes rings privately: a new ring replacing an old one (actions()), openPanel(), and update() when the anchor leaves the room. None of these fire the UI.closeActions hook. G18 would then keep 'ring open' and hold every other prop's glow at 0 until her next tap or a room change.

The ownership table does not say how folded faces are hidden. If layout uses opacity or filter on .mood, status's dim rule (#app.cm-mood #moodbar .mood:not(.cm-awake){opacity:.45}) outranks it and shows folded faces at 45%.
issues.fix: Layout hides folded faces with visibility:hidden, or display:none on .mood. Status may additionally scope its dim to #moodbar:not(.collapsed).

worker_addenda.note: Ports. harness.serve() reuses any server already on a port, whatever directory it serves. Before your first run, and whenever a result looks wrong, check: for p in $(seq <lo> <hi>); do pid=$(pgrep -f "http.server $p --bind"); [ -n "$pid" ] && echo $p $(readlink /proc/$pid/cwd); done. Every line must be your worktree's public/chef-marina; kill any other with kill <pid>. Stale main-tree servers that were in 8850–8929 have been stopped.

Sweeps. Wrap every regress.js and regress-flags.js run in: flock -x /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Krelworld/be5a56b8-2f71-5309-b8d4-9cbd99e75323/scratchpad/audit2/sweep.lock <command>. Before calling any BEHAVES DIFF or flow difference a regression or noise, re-press it A/B against HEAD (port 8847 serves arch/head) under identical conditions; /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Krelworld/be5a56b8-2f71-5309-b8d4-9cbd99e75323/scratchpad/audit2/critic/ab_rows.js is a template. Under load, the stool and wicker 🧗 'perch', the Miles 🤗 'anim' and 'tap floor walks' flip by themselves.

Events. room, screen and activity listeners may run synchronously inside any Clarity.quietFor() or Clarity.sample() call, including inside another item's hook (G2's checkMess hook runs inside AI.update). Keep them cheap and re-entrancy-safe, and never assume they run from the timer.

Switches. Register hooks, ticks, listeners, pointer and appear callbacks and Clarity.css unconditionally at load; the core gates them, so turning a switch ON at run time works. Use `if (Clarity.on.Gn)` at load only for one-time data changes, paired with Clarity.onToggle(id, on => ...) that both applies and restores.

DOM and names:
- Create DOM nodes only while your switch is on.
- Never reuse a game id or class (.act, .pichint, .say, .alertb, .stk-toast, #wishBtn, #reqBtn…); game code and regress.js query them.
- Name new classes and @keyframes cm-gN-… (with your item id) unless the reconcile already names them; class and keyframe names are global and can collide across workers.

Rings close in places the UI.closeActions hook never sees. ui.js closes them through its PRIVATE closeActions when a new ring replaces an old one, in openPanel(), and in update() when the ring's anchor leaves the room. If your item needs 'is a ring open', read document.querySelector('#fx .act').

Insets and core changes:
- Simulated insets (padding in the harness) leave env() at 0. Anything absolutely positioned inside #stage is already offset by env(safe-area-inset-left) through #app's padding; never add env() to its left or right, or her iPhone gets the inset twice and no harness check can show it.
- Core changes from the critic: hook lists are copy-on-write (a hook registered during a call applies from the next call), and Clarity.nudgeX takes opt.dir (+1 or -1).

G6: measure Clarity.hudRects(st, { fresh: true, except: ['give', 'call', 'book', 'dress'] }). The give bubbles, .cm-call and 📒/👗 are in the DOM when the ring opens but are hidden by the ring itself: picHints and nav.js calm both require no .act, and 📒 follows 👗 (see critic/g6_vanish.json). Avoiding them would move Daddy's ring off its usual spot while she carries a dish. Keep wish, req, stop, alert, arrow, pill, map, strip, weather, face and mood. The integration check becomes 'rings avoid wish and req'.

G18: compute 'target ring open' each frame as Clarity.G18.ring && !!document.querySelector('#fx .act'). The ring can close privately (anchor walked out, ring replaced, openPanel). Otherwise every other prop's glow stays at 0 until her next tap or a room change. Add a check: open Daddy's ring, make him walk to another room, and the kitchen's proximity glow returns.
G30: badge only the 2-choice stairs rings, which are never trays. Inside .acttray an .act is position:static, so a badge would anchor to the tray.

G27: never replay from inside the UI.closeActions after-hook. ui.js:52 calls UI.closeActions() before a.fn(), so a choice that opens a screen opens it right after your hook. Measured with 🎨 on the dining table: screenOpen() is false in the hook and true when the tap handler returns (critic/g27_closeorder.js). Schedule with setTimeout(...,0) or the next tick, re-check Clarity.screenOpen(), and otherwise wait for 'screenClose'. The same applies when G2's screenOpen listener calls UI.closeActions(). Also mark your own toasts (e.g. data-cm), because moving one into the fixed fly layer fires appear('.stk-toast') again.

G25: the landscape and short-portrait slot is stage-relative. Use left:122px, not calc(env(safe-area-inset-left) + 122px): #wishBtn and #reqBtn sit inside #stage, which already starts at the inset. Verify 122 px against the widest ✋ chip by measuring #stopBtn (width:auto) with each currentActivity glyph, including 🖼️✋ (G17), 🍽️✋, ♿ and 🧍. The glide ghost must have no id (never cloneNode with id wishBtn or reqBtn) and only cm-g25 classes.

G2: the screenOpen listener's UI.closeActions() also runs the after-hooks of G18 (rings, clears its target) and G27 (dock, must defer). Do not depend on their order. G2's checkMess hook calls quietFor(), which can fire screen and activity listeners synchronously inside AI.update.

G15 dim CSS: do not clobber existing transitions. .mood has transition:transform .1s (its press scale), so use transition:opacity .2s, transform .1s there. Check the other dimmed elements' existing transitions before writing the shorthand.

G15/G24 × G19: in landscape, layout hides a folded column's faces with visibility:hidden. Your dim rule must never make a folded face visible: opacity does not override visibility, but scope the landscape dim to #moodbar:not(.collapsed) .mood to be safe. G23: while a ring is open, .actback covers the stage, so no prop passes Clarity.onCanvas and there are no wiggles while a ring is open. That is acceptable; say so in your results.

G19: hide a folded column's faces only with visibility:hidden (or display:none on .mood), never opacity or filter. Status owns .mood opacity and filter, and its selector outranks yours. After a resize you trigger yourself (onToggle, boot), call Clarity.hudRects(null, { fresh: true }) once; the core drops its 250 ms cache only on window resize and orientationchange.

G4: changeRoom snaps E.camX using the OLD viewW, before your 'room' listener resizes. After resize() on an arrival in or departure from the living room in landscape, re-snap the camera: E.camX = clamp(marina.x - E.viewW / 2, 0, Math.max(0, ROOMS[G.room].w - E.viewW)), then render(). Do this for the room-change resize only, not for TV toggles. Add a check: E.camX equals the snapped value on the first frame after arrival, and no camera glide shows.

G17/G26: use Clarity.nudgeX(box, rects, { dir: Math.sign(roomCentreScreenX - bubbleCentreX) || 0, max: bubbleWidth, bounds: [0, stageW] }) for 'sideways only, toward the room's centre'. G5: hudRects 'strip' entries are the .rb buttons only. If the .say clamp must also clear the dark #roombar backing between and around the buttons, add #roombar's own rect.

G3: on switch-off (onToggle), restore #xFloat's text to ❌; calm.js never resets it. Optional hardening: the lane class is dropped by a MutationObserver microtask. That is safe today, because every canvas screen opens from the room with #panel already hidden. To make it timing-proof, drive the padding from a marker on the classic screen's own .ptop (#panel:has(>.ptop.cm-g3-lane)); the marker vanishes synchronously when a canvas screen replaces #panel's children.

G37/G38: centre the portrait map stack and colour the rows using .fmap, .isowrap, .fmaprow or a wrapper of your own. Never style #panel itself: the screens worker owns it, and G3's landscape lane padding lives on it.

G35: the edge tab is drawn in the drawExitSigns after-hook, i.e. before builder.js's late() pass. In a tree house with the lantern on, or during a nap, thLate's night overlay is drawn over the tab, so screenshot that case. Never re-wrap drawExitSigns. Choose sign spots against the permanent HUD kinds (strip, pill, map, arrow, weather, mood, moodToggle). Treat transient ones (face, give, book, dress, wish, req) as 'skip drawing this frame' only; otherwise a sign can stay undrawn for a whole visit because a face card was talking on arrival.

G36: when the switch flips at run time, the nav.js arrows (icon cached by dataset.to) and floors.js (strip cached per floor) keep the old icons. onToggle must also rewrite .navarrow's icon text and .rb[data-r=nunuroom] / .rb[data-r=treehouse_pine] directly. Checks may reload instead.
